s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
key_facts: Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests negative

raw.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
key_facts: Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests negative

raw.rationale: The presence of a reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis, along with the histologic findings of superficial and deep dermal vascular proliferation and hemosiderin deposits, are consistent with granuloma faciale. The lack of response to topical antifungal cream and the absence of systemic symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions, not a large plaque, and lacks the characteristic vascular proliferation and hemosiderin deposits seen in this case

rejected.label: seborrheic keratosis
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-defined, hyperpigmented lesion with a verrucous surface, which does not match the clinical description of this case

rejected.label: hyperpigmentation
rejected.why: Too nonspecific and does not account for the vascular proliferation and other histologic findings

rejected.label: plaque psoriasis
rejected.why: Typically presents with scaly, erythematous plaques, and the histologic findings in this case do not support a diagnosis of psoriasis
